India also reached 100 in five overs and 50 in 2.2 overs, winning by six wickets to take a commanding 3-0 series lead.

Poyyamozhi was arrested by Chennai Police on October 26 and remanded to judicial custody till November 6. The case involves allegations of collecting money from private school managements in exchange for government recognition and statutory approvals. As the Central Crime Branch continues its investigation, political leaders have weighed in on the arrest and the allegations surrounding the case.

Many individuals, especially children, have endured dire conditions for years amidst the relentless fighting.

The notice was issued after he participated in a protest in Mumbai supporting a political party. Khan's legal team argues that the notice infringes on his constitutional rights and lacks due process. He claims to have lived in India since childhood and holds an Overseas Citizen of India card.

After an arduous wait of three months, the buyer received a different colored model, compounded by issues reported upon pickup. The ruling mandated the dealer to compensate the complainant with Rs 25,000 plus legal fees, with a strict 30-day timeline for compliance to avoid accruing additional interest.

The majority of the removed voters, totaling 65.45 lakh, were identified as permanently shifted. The process concluded with 43.

Kochi nursery fire may be terror plot rehearsal targeting Jews, police suspect
description: Police in Kochi are investigating whether a fire at a horticulture nursery near the Kadavumbhagam Synagogue was a test run for a wider plot. Messages recovered from the accused’s phone allegedly refer to Jewish places of worship and attacks in several cities. Investigators are tracing the senders, following cryptocurrency payments including USDT, and examining reconnaissance visuals and three suspected practice runs in Ernakulam rural. The anti-terror squad is involved, and an NIA handover is under consideration. Police say no organised terror network has yet been established.

title: Kate Middleton shares unseen photo with William, kids after 24-hour charity trek
description: Kate Middleton has shared an unseen photograph featuring Prince William, their three children and mountain rescue volunteers. The picture was taken after she completed Britain's National Three Peaks Challenge in June 2026 to support a cancer charity following her cancer treatment. She posted the photograph on October 25 to mark Mountain Rescue Awareness Day and thank volunteers for their service.

title: Roman emperor's headless torso sells for $34.26m, up from $7.36m in 2010
description: A stunning marble torso of a Roman emperor made headlines at an auction, fetching an astounding $34.26 million, breaking previous records. This remarkable piece, which was sold for only $7.36 million in 2010, showcases its enduring appeal. With its origins in ancient Rome, the sculpture highlights military honor and divine connection, and it has been featured in significant museum displays across the US.

title: 13,800-year-old Alaska campsite reveals hearth and traces of ancient shelter
description: Archaeological research at Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ in Alaska revealed a rich site dating back 13,800 years. The site included stone tools, animal remains, and evidence of a possible shelter. Researchers identified activities such as food processing, toolmaking, and clothing production among early inhabitants. Comparisons with similar tools in Siberia suggest cultural connections across the Bering Land Bridge.

title: Dyslexic campaigner wins UK award for 25 years of helping vulnerable families
description: Andy Willis received the Community Shining Star Award at the Dyslexia Awards 2026 held in Telford. He has been a community campaigner for 25 years, supporting vulnerable individuals and families in Banburyshire. Known as the 'People’s Champion', he founded the Banburyshire Advice Centre to help residents navigate support systems. His extensive voluntary work has contributed to raising awareness of dyslexia and the support available.

title: Jordan strikes Syria after church attack, claims 20-plus Islamic State terrorists killed
description: In retaliation for a tragic church attack that left nine dead in Karak, Jordan's air force launched targeted airstrikes against Islamic State strongholds in southern Syria. Military reports indicate that over 20 militants were neutralized. While the Jordanian military aimed to minimize civilian harm, Syrian sources revealed that the strikes resulted in seven fatalities, including three children, illustrating the complex repercussions of this military engagement.

These experiments involve forcibly separating the babies from their mothers to study the effects of a neurotoxin. Most concerning is that many of these vulnerable infants were reportedly euthanized post-testing. Experts condemn this practice as unethical, highlighting its detrimental impact on the primates' development.

On Ahmedabad to Pune, waiting until the day before departure meant paying 120.5 per cent more than a ticket bought 30 days ahead. On Bengaluru to Chennai, that same wait added just 2.9 per cent. The gap between the two extremes is wide enough to matter for anyone planning travel.

title: Walter Smith's widow picks cancer unit that treated him for £50,000 donation
description: Ethel Smith, honoring the memory of her late husband, former football manager Walter Smith, has generously contributed £50,000 to the cancer unit at Vale of Leven Hospital. This donation aims to enhance the comfort and facilities for patients receiving care. The Emmie Smillie Foundation played a crucial role in facilitating this heartfelt contribution, reflecting the shared experiences of both families affected by cancer.

In response, the Supporting Oyster Aquaculture and Restoration program was launched to convert these excess oysters into valuable resources for habitat restoration. Over 7 million oysters have been sourced from more than 150 farm partners, promoting ecological benefits while supporting local fisheries.

title: Who named Cyclone Arnab and why? Where it will hit, states on alert & preparedness
description: Cyclone Arnab is intensifying and is forecasted to hit the Andhra Pradesh coastline by Wednesday morning. The India Meteorological Department has issued alerts for severe winds and torrential rainfall affecting multiple states. Emergency shelters and control rooms are set up as beach access is prohibited to ensure public safety. Heavy rains are also impacting Odisha and Jharkhand. Residents are urged to stay updated and minimize travel during the cyclone's effects.

title: Scottish survivors start 'Courtrobe' to provide outfits and stylists for court
description: Two sexual assault survivors in Scotland have launched CourtRobe, a campaign to help women feel more confident when giving evidence in court. Sarah Lee, 39, and Kayla Poulton, 36, are seeking clothing donations and shopping vouchers from department stores. The initiative, being developed with the University of Glasgow's Emma Ritch Law Clinic, also aims to provide free personal shopping sessions with trauma-trained retail staff.

Love Patel allegedly used his father's licensed pistol shortly after recording a video. In the video, he expressed emotional distress and addressed his father before the incident. His father, Munna Lal, mentioned that Love experienced stress and had difficulty sleeping at times. Police are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding this unfortunate incident.

Bishnoi had over two million followers across various platforms, which did not translate into electoral support. His role as president of a local cow shelter was also not enough to sway voters.

Despite his achievements, he admitted that managing teams was not his true calling. Moskovitz faced increasing challenges during his tenure due to external social and political upheaval. Many corporate leaders, like Moskovitz, find themselves in management roles without formal training or desire. This phenomenon of the 'accidental manager' has become common in workplaces.

title: US court says detained migrants have no constitutional right to bond hearings
description: The US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit has made a pivotal ruling concerning immigrant detention, involving three men who unlawfully entered the country. The court decided to overturn earlier decisions that allowed them individualized bond hearings while awaiting removal proceedings. This change stirs substantial dialogue on the potential impacts on the constitutional rights of immigrants facing detention without due process.
